hints: Look carefully at where the thick stage micrometer lines line up on the fine 0 to 100 scale, how many fine graticule divisions fit between two thick lines?
Remember each thick line interval is 0.1 mm, convert that to micrometres first, then divide by the number of graticule divisions to get micrometres per graticule division.
walkthrough:
**Work out what the diagram is showing**

Look at the overlap. The thick vertical lines are the stage micrometer, 0.1 mm apart. The fine 0 to 100 scale is the eyepiece graticule.

From the image, one stage interval (thick line to next thick line) covers 40 eyepiece graticule divisions, for example from about 11 to about 51, and from about 51 to about 91.

**Calibrate one graticule division**

First convert the known stage distance to micrometres:
$$0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.1 \times 1000 = 100 \, \mu\text{m}$$

So 40 graticule divisions = 100 micrometres.
$$1 \text{ graticule division} = 100 \div 40 = 2.5 \, \mu\text{m}$$

**Apply to the lymphocyte**

The lymphocyte is $10 \, \mu\text{m}$ in diameter.
$$\text{number of divisions} = 10 \div 2.5 = 4$$

So 4 graticule divisions will just cover it.

options.A: 1 division is only 2.5 micrometres, far too small to cover a 10 micrometre lymphocyte.
options.B: 4 divisions x 2.5 micrometres per division = 10 micrometres, exactly the lymphocyte diameter.
options.C: 10 divisions would be 25 micrometres, more than twice the size of the lymphocyte.
options.D: 20 divisions would be 50 micrometres, about five lymphocytes wide, so much too large.
